task.title: Fix web queue lost updates: detail form expectedHead and the dead stale-write re-base
task.description:
The optimistic web mutation queue has two divergences from its design that cause user-visible lost updates in exactly the multi-writer scenario a shared beta creates. Neither is recorded in the divergence notes from commit 7d48f3e. Both verified by reading internal/webui/assets/index.html at commit c453596.

1. The task detail form never sends expectedHead, so it is silent last-writer-wins across every field.
The submit handler builds `values` from title, description, status, priority, and labels (index.html:1316-1328) with no expectedHead, and it sends every field on every save. A form opened before a teammates change reverts that change on save: their title edit is reverted by your description-only save. This is precisely the "browser holding a board from four seconds ago silently overwrites" scenario the design used to motivate expectedHead. Server support already exists and is correct (updateTaskRequest.ExpectedHead at internal/webui/handler.go:198; requireExpectedHead at internal/core/service.go:551-561). Only the position route wires the client half (index.html:1947-1951).

2. The stale-write re-base the design promises is unreachable, so every intent queued behind a conflict fails in turn.
The design doc states at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-optimistic-web-mutation-queue-design.md:146-147 that a stale write "re-bases the queues head from that refresh so the intents behind it retry against current truth instead of failing identically." drainIntents sets `entry.inFlight = true` for the entire drain and clears it only in the finally block (index.html:1494-1523), while adoptRefreshedHeads skips any entry with inFlight set (index.html:1566-1572). A non-empty draining queue therefore always has inFlight true, and the head can never be re-based while it matters. In the catch branch the loop calls refresh() but never updates entry.head, so the next intent is sent with the same stale head and 409s in turn. The result is that all queued intents behind a conflict are dropped, not only the ones that depended on the failed intent as the in-code comment claims. No durable corruption: the board converges to server truth on the next poll.

This went unnoticed because the two client tests the designs Testing section promises do not exist. internal/webui/handler_test.go has TestHandlerClientRendersAPlacementBeforeItsResponseAndSurvivesAPoll (:4887) and TestHandlerClientSendsOneTasksIntentsSeriallyThreadingTheHead (:4968), and no test for "a failed intent rolls back and leaves a later intent standing" or "a stale-write response rolls back, refreshes, and reports".

Related edge from commit eaaee47, which is otherwise sound: refresh() never re-renders an open detail route (index.html:1845-1852 updates relationships only), so if a pending intent fails while the detail form is open the form keeps showing the optimistic status, and saving persists the failed optimistic value as a real edit.

Acceptance:
- The detail form sends expectedHead on update, and a save whose head is stale is refused rather than clobbering.
- Consider sending only changed fields so an unrelated concurrent edit is not reverted even when heads agree.
- A stale-write during a drain re-bases the queue head from the refresh so intents behind it retry against current truth, or the design doc is corrected to state that they are dropped and the in-code comment is corrected with it.
- The two client tests the design promises exist and fail against the current behavior.
- An open detail form reflects a pending intent that later failed.
- docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-optimistic-web-mutation-queue-design.md matches shipped behavior, and the divergence notes from 7d48f3e are extended with whichever of these remains.

## Downstream

WB-01KZC3PGA0QCXKDQ936VPM67D5 (reconcile the board renderer) depends on this ticket. That work restructures render() and the rerender path this ticket also touches, so landing the queue correctness fixes first means the render path is rewritten once against settled semantics rather than twice. Keep that in mind when changing drainIntents, adoptRefreshedHeads, or the detail-form submit: the follow-on will move the rendering underneath them, not the intent lifecycle itself.
